q_en: When you meet an Arabic word, what job is it doing?
Where does this word come from, and can I guess its meaning?
Is the speaker talking about one particular thing, or any thing?
Is this person or thing male or female?
How many people or things are there: one, two or many?
Which small word can stand in for a person or thing?
Which word points to the person or thing: this, that, these, those?
What is the question asking for?

title_en: What is it about, and what is said about it?
q_en: Can a sentence say something without a verb?
Does the second word match the first?
Is it a full sentence, or only a pointing phrase?
Is “noun + adjective” one idea, or a full sentence?
How do I say who someone is, or what they are like?
How do I say where something is?
How do I ask a question, and how do I answer it?
How do I say that something is NOT so?

title_en: The past verb: he and she
q_en: What happened, and who did it?
Who or what is doing the action?

title_en: The past verb: I, you, we, they
q_en: Who did it, when there is no doer word? The ending tells you.
The boy did something. What did he do it to?
Did it happen already, or is it happening now?
Who is doing it: I, you, he, she, we or they?
How do I tell someone to do something, or not to do it?
How do I say that something WAS so?
How do I say that someone did not, will not or does not do something?
How is this noun joined to the rest of the sentence?

title_en: My, your, his: pronouns on the end
q_en: Whose is it? Who is the little ending on this word?
Whose is it? What is this thing “of”?

title_en: The pronoun on the end of a verb
q_en: Who or what was it done to?
How does the writer join one idea to the next?
How can a sentence tell us more about a person or thing: “the man WHO wrote…”?
How do we say “because”, “if / when” and “indeed”?
How do I read “three books”, “every student”, “some of the people”?
Can I follow a whole story: who did what, to whom, and in what order?
Who is speaking, what are they asking or telling, and what do the small words (not, do, ?) change?
What is this short saying of the Prophet ﷺ telling me?

title_en: A story in the Qur’an: sūrat al-Fīl
q_en: Who did what, and what happened in the end?

title_en: Qur’an: a promise, a reminder, a prayer
q_en: What is this verse doing: promising, reminding, commanding or asking?

title_en: Read and understand: the five questions
q_en: Can I take any Arabic sentence and work out what it means?
Why does the last letter of a word keep changing?
This word means “many”: which word is the one?

title_en: Who did it? Nobody says: the passive
q_en: The door was opened. By whom? The sentence does not say. How does Arabic say it?

title_en: A doubled middle letter: Form II
q_en: Why is there a shadda in the middle of this verb, and what does it change?

title_en: Reading day 1: the formulas of the Rātib and where they come from
q_en: I know these words by ear. Can I read them, understand them and say where they come from?

title_en: An alif after the first letter, or a hamza before it: Forms III and IV
title_ar: أَلِفٌ بَعْدَ الْحَرْفِ الْأَوَّلِ أَوْ هَمْزَةٌ قَبْلَهُ
q_en: Why do some verbs have an alif after the first letter (سَافَرَ) and others a hamza before it (أَرْسَلَ)?

title_en: تَـ at the front: Forms V and VI
q_en: Why does this verb begin with تَـ?

title_en: Extra letters at the front: Forms VII, VIII and X
title_ar: حُرُوفٌ زَائِدَةٌ فِي أَوَّلِ الْفِعْلِ: اِنْـ، ـتـ، اِسْتَـ
q_en: What are the extra letters before the root of this verb?

title_en: A letter that doubles, a hamza that hides
q_en: This verb has a shadda, and that one has lost its hamza. Where did the letters go?

title_en: Reading day: a ḥadīth with its chain
q_en: Where does the chain end, and where do the words begin?

title_en: The middle letter hides: hollow verbs
q_en: Where did the middle letter go?

title_en: A weak first or last letter
q_en: Why does the first letter vanish in يَجِدُ and the last letter change in دَعَوْتُ?

title_en: Odd ones: verbs that break the pattern
q_en: What do I do with the verbs that do not follow the usual shape?

title_en: One root, one family of words
q_en: How do I tell the doer, the one done-to and the action name of one root?
What does the shape of a noun tell me before I know the word?
How do I find a word I do not know in a dictionary?
Which small words change the ending of the words after them?
How do I say in what state someone did something?
Some words ending in ـًا are not the doer or the thing acted on. What are they telling me?
Some verbs act on two things at once. And what does لَا do before a noun, as in لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ?
A page that lists things: what is being counted, and which is the first, the second, the third?
How do I read “O …!” and “By God!”: who is being called, and what happens to the word?
Which word takes someone out of a sentence, and what happens to the word after it?

title_en: Names in a chain: son of, titles, kunya
q_en: How do I read a long name: who is whose son, which words are titles, and what are the endings?

title_en: A verb and its little word: one unit
q_en: Which little word does this verb take, and does it change the meaning?

title_en: Reading day 5: advice (do, do not, if … then)
q_en: How do I read a text that tells me what to do?

title_en: Little words of time, place and degree
q_en: What do the little words always, mostly, never, very, also and only add to a sentence?
How do “as for … then”, “either … or”, “when”, “while”, “whenever” and “until” tie sentences together?
In “the book that I read”, which word points back to the book, and what do we do when there is no “that”?
Why does the last vowel of a present verb change after some little words?

title_en: If … then: the condition and its answer
q_en: If this happens, what follows? How do I find the condition and its answer?
How do I read a number, a date or a time in an old book?

title_ar: الْقُرْآنُ مَعَ التَّفْسِيرِ: أَيْ وَيَعْنِي وَالْمُرَادُ
q_en: Which words are the verse, and which words explain it?

title_en: A ḥadīth with its chain and its commentary
q_en: Where does the chain end, where do the words begin, and where does the commentary start?

title_en: A short ḥadīth: condition and reward
q_en: What must a person do, and what does he get for it?

title_en: Fiqh: matn, sharḥ and the ruling
q_en: What is the ruling, and what is it about?
What is a creed made of, and how do I read a line of verse?
How does a teacher’s counsel speak, and what do its four little frames say?

title_en: A page of advice: the long sentence
q_en: How do I read a long sentence, and follow the thread of the argument from line to line?

title_en: The litany whole: Wird and Rātib
q_en: How do I read the whole litany at speed: what is said, how many times, and which part is the Qur’an?
How do I read a page of mawlid prose, where the clauses rhyme, the nouns hang in long chains, and the vowels begin to disappear?
How do I read a poem: where does each bayt break, how does the rhyme work, and why are some words in a strange order?

title_en: The sīra: born, grew up, travelled
q_en: How do I read the story of a life, section by section: who, when, where, and what came next?

title_en: A scholar’s life-entry and a classical letter
q_en: How do I read a scholar’s biography entry, and the opening and closing of a classical letter?

title_en: The majlis record: who is speaking?
q_en: In a record of a majlis, whose words am I reading: the writer’s or the teacher’s? Which little formulas tell me?

title_en: A fatwā, a sermon, a will: three frames
q_en: Who asks and who answers in a fatwā? How does a sermon begin and end? What does a will say, and to whom?

title_en: The grammar primer: the names of the signs
q_en: What does a text about grammar call the signs I have been reading since Lesson 1?

title_en: Level 8 checkpoint: a recorded lesson, and every kind of text
q_en: Can I read a lesson that was spoken and written down, and tell what kind of text any page is?
What happened, where and when? Who did it, if anyone is named?
What does this sign, form, label or e-mail want from me?
What am I asked to do, and in what order?
What is being offered, at what price, when, and what am I asked to do?

title_en: Fable and classical story: how a tale is told
q_en: How does a tale begin, move and end, and who is speaking?

title_en: Proverbs and a line of poetry
q_en: How do I read a saying with no verb, or a verse whose words are turned around?
How does a reference book say what a thing is, and how do I find the word it is explaining?
How do I read a history or a life: what happened, in what order, and why?
Who is travelling, from where to where, and how long did it take?
Who is asking, who is answering, and which words are local?
What are the fixed phrases of a contract, a waqf deed and a research abstract, and what does each part say?
How does a modern story show what is seen, what is thought, what is felt and what is said, all in one passage?

title_en: A day of reading: the capstone
q_en: Can I read any text, of any kind, and understand it?
